title: Hengsheng Luthier Workshop
premise: A long luthier drama amid shavings and wood scent. A-Xian and A-Hui are easily confused; the spruce top plate goes intact_unjoined→cracked→butterfly_patched; the instrument cart must be avoided after destruction; soundpost/caliper/tuning-fork count memory, false friends, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.prime_on_duty: Gu Heng the luthier in his fifties, half-frame glasses, linen apron, sawdust on his cuffs, focused expression.
states.weary_injured: The same Gu Heng: apron torn, right hand bandaged, leaning on a wooden cane, glasses still on his nose.
states.retired_curtain: Gu Heng has left the workshop; only his linen apron and glasses remain—he no longer appears.

states.young_apprentice: Apprentice A-Xian at fourteen or fifteen, indigo headscarf, gray cloth short jacket, bright stubborn eyes.
states.adult_successor: A-Xian in his twenties, still in indigo headscarf, upright and steady.

states.intact_unjoined: A spruce top plate with tight grain, surface planed mirror-smooth, join lines marked at the edges.
states.cracked: The same spruce top plate now cracked; fine splits along the grain, join lines misaligned.
states.butterfly_patched: The spruce top plate crack closed with butterfly inlays; patch pieces clearly visible.

states.intact: A luthier notebook in cowhide cover, recording wood moisture and arch data.
states.glue_stained: The same luthier notebook soaked through with fish glue; cover sticky, ink blurred.

states.intact: A wooden instrument cart, bed lined with velvet, rail stamped with a small 'Gu' mark.
states.overturned_wrecked: The instrument cart overturned on the slope; bed shattered, axle broken, reduced to wreckage.

states.young_rival: Youth A-Hui, face very like A-Xian's, cream-white neck scarf, ebony hairpin at the temple, bold expression.
states.disguised_anew: Disguised anew, A-Hui still wears the cream-white neck scarf; hairpin swapped to black, expression deeper.

segments.action: At dusk, Gu Heng enters the shavings workshop and runs his hand over the spruce top plate on the bench.
Five vernier calipers hang on the tool board; Gu Heng zeroes each one.
Two brass tuning forks hang under the drying-gallery eaves; Gu Heng taps them to let them ring.
Gu Heng circles the bench checking whether the plane irons are rolled.
Gu Heng gazes through the window at the fading string shadows in the instrument drying gallery.
Under the lamp the spruce top plate shows tight grain; Gu Heng feels the moisture with his fingertip.
Gu Heng sits on a wooden stool in the workshop corner for a brief rest.
Gu Heng opens the luthier notebook and records the day's top-plate arch.
Gu Heng draws a thickness-distribution curve in the luthier notebook.
Gu Heng closes the luthier notebook and puts it back in the bench chest.
The join lines at the spruce top plate edges are clear; Gu Heng nods.
Gu Heng wipes sawdust from the notebook cover with a dry cloth.
In the morning instrument drying gallery, Gu Heng greets young A-Xian arriving with the instrument cart.
A-Xian steadies the cart and smooths the velvet lining flat again.
Gu Heng points to three soundpost blanks on the bench corner and teaches A-Xian to read the wood grain.
A-Xian crouches by a gallery post, curious about the hanging half-finished bodies.
Gu Heng explains the bass-bar line; A-Xian listens and nods seriously.
A-Xian looks back at the wooden instrument cart, eyes full of care.
Gu Heng has A-Xian practice measuring plate thickness with calipers first.
In the bustling instrument-street shopfront, A-Hui in a cream-white neck scarf looks up from behind the counter.

segments.action: In the rainy season, Gu Heng in the shavings workshop sweeps damp shavings to the stove to dry.
Gu Heng brushes sawdust from the caliper jaws.
At dawn, Gu Heng in the instrument drying gallery checks the hygrometer.
Gu Heng hangs his raincoat on a gallery post and listens to rain on the glass roof.
In midsummer, Gu Heng opens the workshop skylight to drive out glue fumes.
Gu Heng checks the fish-glue pot temperature so it does not thicken too much.
When autumn wind rises, Gu Heng pulls cover cloths off the outdoor half-finished bodies.
Gu Heng tries a new arch code on a blank page of the luthier notebook.
On a frosty night, Gu Heng lights an oil lamp and checks the flashlight battery.
Gu Heng wraps the top plate in a blanket to prevent night cracking.
On a heavy-snow day, Gu Heng sweeps thin snow from the old workshop porch steps.
Gu Heng breathes on his hands and tightens the red cord on the soundpost blanks.
In early spring, Gu Heng trims the ivy on the porch.
Gu Heng oils all five calipers one by one.
Gu Heng posts a new schedule on the workshop wall.
Around the Dragon Boat Festival, Gu Heng smokes the wood store with mugwort to repel insects.
Gu Heng re-planes the end faces of the soundpost blanks.
Gu Heng paces alone in the instrument drying gallery, memorizing bass-bar positions.
After the rain stops, Gu Heng pushes open the workshop door and listens to eaves drip into an iron bucket.
Gu Heng swaps worn sandpaper for fresh.
Another dusk, Gu Heng sits by the spruce top plate listening to the radio.
Gu Heng gets up at night to refill the humidifier.
Gu Heng hangs fresh horsehair strings to straighten.
Gu Heng wipes the 'Hengsheng' porch plaque.
Gu Heng checks the instrument cart velvet for holes.
Gu Heng marks the f-hole position on the drawing.
Gu Heng wrings out a glue-stained rag and hangs it up.
On a full-moon night, Gu Heng leans on the gallery railing at the bodies, varnish silver in the light.
Gu Heng organizes the tool board so all caliper jaws face the same way.
Gu Heng writes a new season's luthier notes on the notebook flyleaf.
Gu Heng polishes both tuning forks.
Gu Heng listens to trial playing from the shopfront and keeps planing the top plate thinner.
Gu Heng glues a split wooden wedge back together.
Gu Heng stacks spare ribs in the workshop corner.
Gu Heng shuts doors and windows against sudden night humidity swings.
Another Qingming, Gu Heng places a bunch of wildflowers on the porch.
Gu Heng rolls the drawing into a tube and binds it with a rubber band.
Gu Heng taps a tuning fork; the tone rings clear.
Gu Heng sits silently in the workshop, listening to shavings fall for a long while.
Gu Heng cuts worn indigo cloth into rags for later use.
At daybreak, Gu Heng patrols the instrument drying gallery; the instrument cart stands at the gallery mouth.
Gu Heng crouches to check lubrication on the instrument cart axle.
Gu Heng walks to the bench corner; the same three soundpost blanks are still bound with red cord.
A red delivery tricycle passes outside the gallery, tin bed—not the Gu family's wooden cart.
Gu Heng stands in the instrument drying gallery and records the hygrometer reading.
Gu Heng hangs the damp velvet cloth on a gallery rack.
Gu Heng brushes shavings from his sleeve and looks back toward the workshop lights.
After Grain Rain, Gu Heng in the instrument drying gallery teaches a new apprentice to read tight vs loose grain.
Gu Heng drapes the dried cover cloths back over the bodies.
In summer heat, Gu Heng lays a damp cloth beside the fish-glue pot to cool it.
Gu Heng checks the instrument cart and moves the damp velvet to the upper layer.
On an autumn night, Gu Heng under the oil lamp mends loose pages of the luthier notebook.
Gu Heng sends all five calipers out for calibration in rotation.
At first snow, Gu Heng sweeps a narrow path at the old workshop porch threshold.
Gu Heng restacks spare pine boards neatly.
Gu Heng listens to a tuning fork's soft ring and keeps revising the schedule.
Gu Heng opens the gallery door to let a cross-breeze carry away glue smell.
Gu Heng hangs a rain awning on the porch.
Gu Heng puts chipped plane irons into an iron box.
Gu Heng dreams of the top plate cracking, wakes, and writes it in the notebook.
Gu Heng rinses calipers with clean water.
Gu Heng wipes the schedule clean and posts it again.
Gu Heng pulls weeds from mortar cracks in the gallery posts.
Gu Heng hangs calipers back on the tool board; the numbered tags have faded.
Gu Heng takes a last look at the spruce top plate crack before switching off the light.
Gu Heng folds the indigo headscarf the apprentice left in the workshop.
Gu Heng hears the shopfront lock at closing time and gets up to bolt the door.
Gu Heng dries gloves by the charcoal brazier.
Gu Heng moves the tuning forks aside to show the freshly repaired gallery eaves.
Gu Heng dries the humidity-test paper strips.
Gu Heng draws a thickness comparison on the notebook's last page.
Gu Heng murmurs tomorrow's top plate to join and steps out onto the porch.
Gu Heng pushes the instrument cart to the wall and clears shavings floor space.
Gu Heng hears a distant night watch drum and blows out the oil lamp.
Another rainy night, Gu Heng alone watches over the top plate until dawn.
Gu Heng trial-fits a newly arrived rosewood end block.
On a storm night, workshop humidity spikes; wood pops and creaks.
The bench trembles slightly in the shaking.
A faint snap—the spruce top plate splits along the grain.

segments.action: Outside the gallery comes String merchant Old Qiao, peg bag on his back, build like Gu Heng's.
The Association supervisor arrives too, gray suit and chest badge, standing beside Gu Heng to talk.
The supervisor points at the red delivery tricycle and asks whether it belongs to the Hengsheng workshop.
The supervisor leaves; Gu Heng alone remains in the instrument drying gallery.
Old Qiao unloads a crate of strings and bows farewell.
At the shopfront comes girl Xiao Zheng in a light-brown headscarf—at a glance somewhat like young A-Xian.
Xiao Zheng tries wiping a bow; Gu Heng shakes his head—she is not A-Xian after all.
Xiao Zheng lowers her head shyly and tightens her headscarf.
Years later at dusk, Gu Heng with bandaged right hand stands on his cane in the old workshop porch.
